stories.head: Tealium + Jev: Real-time AI decisioning without the LLM cost
stories.plain: Tealium's CDP triggers a lightweight AI decision model called Jev — not a full LLM — to pick the next best action after a cart abandonment. This matters because it shows a practical, cheaper path to real-time agentic decisioning that avoids the steep inference costs stopping most marketers from scaling AI personalization.

stories.head: Pega CFO: Biggest AI budget waste is automating routine rules-based work
stories.plain: Pega's CFO Ken Stillwell breaks down where enterprise AI spend goes wrong: companies keep paying AI to do work that simple rules engines could handle cheaply. He offers proxy ROI measures and a framework for when to kill an AI project. Essential reading for anyone approving or pitching an AI budget.

stories.head: Agentic media buying must bake malware guardrails into optimization logic
stories.plain: As AI agents autonomously place and adjust ad buys, traffic-quality and security signals risk being ignored by optimizers chasing cheap conversions. This piece argues that malware and fraud detection must become first-class inputs in agentic campaign logic — a governance gap that could cost brands money and reputation if left unaddressed.

stories.head: FouAnalytics and fraud0 launch AI agent that auto-recovers wasted Google Ads spend
stories.plain: An AI agent now detects invalid traffic in Google Ads and automatically files and recovers refunds for large advertisers — no manual claim process needed. This is a concrete example of an agentic system acting on a financial goal end-to-end, and it signals how ad-quality accountability is being automated at enterprise scale.

stories.head: Verndale launches AI visibility and content supply-chain services for GEO
stories.plain: Verndale is selling a service that audits whether AI assistants mention, recommend, and accurately describe a brand — then fixes the content gaps. As AI-generated answers replace traditional search results, this kind of GEO service is becoming a new line item in marketing budgets, changing how content strategy is planned and measured.

stories.head: Tealium + Jev demo: real-time AI decisioning after cart abandonment without LLM cost
stories.plain: Tealium's CDP calls Jev, a lightweight AI decision model, to pick the next-best action the moment a shopper abandons a cart — no large language model needed. This matters because it shows a practical path to real-time agentic decisioning at scale without the compute bill that usually comes with LLM-based personalization.

stories.head: Pega CFO: the biggest AI budget waste is paying AI to do routine rules-based work
stories.plain: Pega's CFO Ken Stillwell argues that most enterprise AI spend is misdirected at automating tasks that simple rules could handle cheaper. He outlines proxy ROI measures and a kill-switch discipline for AI projects — directly useful for anyone buying or governing marketing AI this budget cycle.

stories.head: Algolia acquires Velou to bring AI product-graph intelligence to search, recommendations and agents
stories.plain: Algolia is buying Velou's AI-powered catalog enrichment and retail taxonomy to power its 18,000-customer platform. Product understanding becomes a shared layer beneath search, personalization and AI agents — meaning the same catalog intelligence serves human shoppers and autonomous buying agents simultaneously.

stories.head: OpenAI adds visual ad formats to ChatGPT and faces bot-inflation problem
stories.plain: ChatGPT ads are expanding with image-based formats and improved measurement tools, but bots are already inflating click-through rates. This changes how media budgets inside AI interfaces should be planned and measured — and adds a new fraud-governance layer marketers must account for.

stories.head: Classic marketing automation is dead: agentic, human-in-the-loop systems are next
stories.plain: Rule-based 'if-this-then-that' automation is being replaced by autonomous AI systems that set their own priorities and act without per-step human approval. The piece maps the shift and argues for deliberate human-in-the-loop design as the key governance guardrail when buying or building next-generation marketing platforms.

month.skicker: 30-day synthesis · the shape underneath the feed

themes.head: Classic automation is dead — agentic orchestration takes over
body: Rule-based marketing automation is being displaced by AI agents that can plan, decide, and act across channels without a human scripting every step. Cisco's agentic collaboration launch, Braze's expansion from content to campaign operations, and Validity's MCP connector all point to the same pivot: the workflow is no longer a flowchart, it's a delegation.

The risk that comes with this shift is equally new. PropellerAds warns that agentic media buying opens a direct route for malware injection, meaning guardrails must be built before scale is pursued. Marketers who hand over execution to agents without governance frameworks are trading one kind of inefficiency for a potentially costlier one.

themes.head: The AI search visibility race reshapes content strategy
body: Answer Engine Optimisation is forcing a fundamental rethink of how brands produce and distribute content. Getfluence & OtterlyAI, Verndale's AI Visibility services, and Algolia's Velou acquisition all treat being found by AI models as a first-class objective alongside traditional search rankings. Visual SEO strategies for AI search are now a distinct discipline, not an afterthought.

OpenAI adding visuals to ChatGPT ads signals that the AI search layer will itself become an advertising surface, compressing the time brands have to establish organic authority before paid competition arrives. Companies that delay building structured, machine-readable brand narratives risk being invisible at the exact moment AI assistants are consulted by their customers.
ev: MarTech AI · Visual SEO for AI search

themes.head: Enterprise AI readiness gap is the real budget problem
body: Pega's CFO Ken Stillwell highlights that the biggest AI cost is not model access but AI doing routine, rules-based work that should have been eliminated years ago. Typeface's CRO echoes this, arguing that most enterprises are buying AI on top of unresolved data and process debt rather than transforming the underlying operation.

The practical implication is a two-speed market: organisations that prepared their data infrastructure and content supply chains are capturing compounding returns, while unprepared ones are spending on AI that merely automates their existing inefficiencies. Verndale's new content supply chain services and Treasure AI's dual-headache platform both treat infrastructure readiness as the prerequisite product.
ev: Agile Brand · Pega AI budget reality

themes.head: Brand measurement loses its old source of truth
body: As AI intermediaries sit between brands and buyers, traditional click-and-conversion attribution breaks down because the AI assistant, not the ad, now shapes the purchase consideration. MarTech's call for a new measurement source of truth, combined with Bazaarvoice's argument that ads can buy placement but not belief, points to a credibility-and-trust metric rising to sit alongside performance metrics.

Ad fraud compounds the problem: FouAnalytics & fraud0's automated Google Ads refund partnership reveals just how much budget is silently wasted on invalid traffic. Marketers rebuilding measurement frameworks need to account simultaneously for AI-intermediated attribution loss and persistent fraud erosion — two forces that together can make campaign ROI look falsely healthy or falsely poor.
ev: Agile Brand · Ads can't buy belief

themes.head: AI tools embed into existing workflows, not separate portals
body: The dominant product pattern of the month is AI capability surfacing inside tools marketers already open every day rather than requiring a new login. Validity's MCP connector brings email intelligence into existing stacks; Salesforce's Listen Labs acquisition embeds AI customer research natively; Stensul personalises enterprise email at scale from within familiar composition environments.

This embed-not-replace strategy lowers adoption friction but raises integration stakes — every new connector is also a new data-sharing agreement and a new failure point. Marketers evaluating these offers should ask not just whether the AI feature works, but whether the underlying data contract is sound and whether the vendor ecosystem can be governed coherently as agent-to-agent calls multiply.
ev: MarTech AI · Salesforce buys Listen Labs
Agile Brand · Stensul personalisation at scale

month.takeaway: Across every product launch and partnership this month, the underlying pressure is the same: AI is collapsing the distance between data, decision, and action — and marketers who have not resolved their infrastructure debt, measurement models, and governance frameworks will find that speed amplifies their existing weaknesses rather than hiding them.
